---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS/macOS. Marketing supplied a screenshot with tiny tagline text, simulated platform corner mask, baked-in drop shadow and a seasonal badge occupying half the mark. No final artwork exists.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

- [Accessibility](.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md)
- [App icons](.topics/apple-hig-app-icons/SKILL.md)

## Completion evidence

Report the concrete decisions or changes, their source support, and which checks
passed, failed or were not executed. A source citation or a list of links is not
the requested work product. Retain platform exceptions and unresolved source
conflicts; the absence of a platform subsection does not establish support.

name: apple-hig-app-icons
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an app icon, its layered construction, platform mask, small-size identity, or appearance variants.

# Preserve an icon's identity through system treatments

Read [App icons](../../references/app-icons.md). Inspect the actual artwork/layers, target platforms, smallest appearances, and requested mode: design, review, or adaptation. If only a flat image exists, distinguish visible composition findings from unverified layer behavior. Produce the requested icon specification, revised assets, or scoped review; preserve existing tools unless a platform export requires another one.

Choose one identifiable concept and remove detail that cannot survive reduction. Decide which shapes need distinct foreground layers and which can remain a quiet opaque background. Supply unmasked artwork: the system supplies the rounded or circular mask. Leave highlights, bevels, and shadow treatment to the system unless an intentional custom effect has been checked for conflicts.

Select construction by platform. Use the guide's Icon Composer workflow for iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS and image-stack workflow for tvOS/visionOS; consult its canvas/variant table rather than copying dimensions from a different platform. tvOS needs crop-safe layered foreground content during focus motion; visionOS should avoid a background hollow that system lighting could make appear raised. A Watch icon's black background must separate from surrounding display black. Keep identifying features stable through applicable dark, clear, tinted, or alternate variants.

**Before → decision → after:** A book-club icon is a pre-rounded screenshot containing a tiny “New” badge and five book titles. Small-size identity needs one silhouette. The corrected specification uses unmasked layers with a simple overlapping-book mark, an opaque background, and stable mark placement across appearance variants; temporary text moves into app content.

Deliver the layer/variant inventory with the corrected artwork or review. Fail if system masking removes the identifying mark, reduction erases it, or focus/lighting changes its intended shape. Actual Icon Composer/device previews are needed to establish parallax, material effects, and platform export quality; a raster mockup alone does not verify them.

For supporting image formats use [Images](../apple-hig-images/SKILL.md); for in-app glyphs instead of launcher identity use [Icons](../apple-hig-icons/SKILL.md); for brand consistency use [Branding](../apple-hig-branding/SKILL.md).

# App icons Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An app icon identifies the product in launchers, search, notifications, settings, and sharing contexts. Keep its identity recognizable across platforms and sizes. ## Layer design Layering lets the system add responsive depth. iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS use a background plus one or more foreground layers with Liquid Glass highlights, refraction, and translucency that can change across releases. tvOS uses 2–5 layers for focus elevation, lighting, sway, and parallax. visionOS uses one background plus 1–2 foreground layers, with shadows and alpha-based embossed depth. Create foreground artwork in a design tool. For iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS, use Icon Composer to define the background, place layers, tune and preview effects, annotate default/dark/mono variants, and export to Xcode. For tvOS/visionOS, assemble an Xcode image stack and preview parallax with Apple’s tools. Use crisp foreground edges rather than feathering. Explore translucent overlapping parts to reveal depth; importing opaque shapes then adjusting opacity in Composer helps test interactions with system effects. A simple solid or gradient background usually needs no imported image; imported backgrounds must be opaque and fill the canvas. Prefer SVG or PDF vectors with artwork and text outlined; use lossless PNG for raster content and mesh gradients. ## Icon shape Supply unmasked square layers for iOS/iPadOS/macOS, which receive rounded-rectangle masks, and for visionOS/watchOS, which receive circular masks. tvOS needs landscape rectangular layers. Pre-masking causes poor highlights and jagged edges. Center essential content, especially inside circular masks, using Apple’s production-template grids. ## Design Choose one distinctive, simple concept with few shapes and a quiet background. Fine detail, thin lines, and sharp corners lose clarity at small sizes or under highlights and shadows. Keep the core design consistent across platforms. Filled overlapping shapes can create useful depth. Use text only when essential to identity; tiny, unlocalizable icon text is often redundant with the app name. Avoid instructional or temporary words. In tvOS, put essential text on the foreground layer to prevent parallax cropping. Prefer simplified illustrations over detailed photos, screenshots, or replicas of standard controls. Do not reproduce Apple hardware in icons. ## Visual effects Let the system supply dynamic highlights, shadows between layers, bevels, blur, and glow. If intentional custom effects are necessary, test for conflicts in Icon Composer, Device Hub, and on hardware. Group related layers when an effect should apply to the group; Composer exposes extra Liquid Glass tuning for groups. ## Appearances Keep identifying features stable across default, dark, clear, and tinted appearances; missing variants can be generated by the system. Dark designs are subdued and clear/tinted ones more restrained still. Start dark variants from the default palette with complementary colors and restrained brightness; colored backgrounds often improve contrast. Alternate icons may be offered through app settings on iOS/iPadOS/tvOS and compatible apps in visionOS. Keep alternatives recognizably related to the app. Alternate iOS/iPadOS icons also need dark, clear, and tinted variants; all icons and variants remain subject to app review. ## Platform considerations No extra platform rules are listed for iOS, iPadOS, or macOS. ### tvOS Leave a safe zone around primary art because focus movement and enlargement crop edges, particularly in foreground layers. The necessary safe zone depends on layer depth, image dimensions, and motion. ### visionOS Avoid background shapes intended to look recessed or hollow: system highlights and shadows can make them appear raised. ### watchOS Lighten black backgrounds enough to separate the icon from the display’s black surroundings. ## Specifications |Platform|Unmasked canvas|System result|Pixels|Construction|Appearance variants| |---|---|---|---:|---|---| |iOS, iPadOS, macOS|Square|Rounded square|1024 × 1024|Layered|Default, dark, clear light/dark, tinted light/dark| |tvOS|Landscape rectangle|Rounded rectangle|800 × 480|Layered parallax|No variants listed| |visionOS|Square|Circle|1024 × 1024|Layered 3D|No variants listed| |watchOS|Square|Circle|1088 × 1088|Layered|No variants listed| The system creates smaller settings/notification variants. Supported profiles are sRGB, Gray Gamma 2.2, and Display P3; the source excludes visionOS from its Display P3 icon-support list. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 8, 2026, June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024, January 31, 2024, June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.

name: apple-hig-branding
description: Use when expressing a brand through an Apple-platform interface, or reviewing branded colors, typography, language, logos, and customized controls.
---

# Express the brand without displacing the task

Read [Branding](../../references/branding.md). Inspect brand assets, product voice, actual screen hierarchy, and the requested design/review/adaptation scope. Identify what a person is trying to do and which identity cues genuinely help recognize this product. The decision inventory below is application advice; use the guide for Apple's stated constraints.

Separate identity from interaction convention. Preserve familiar navigation, control meaning, size, and behavior while choosing a distinctive tone, accent, content treatment, or heading style. If a proposal replaces a conventional symbol or moves a familiar action solely for branding, restore the convention and express character elsewhere.

Choose where emphasis belongs. Reserve accent color for meaningful actions/states; richer brand imagery may live in scrolling content rather than every glass control. If a custom font is essential, retain it where it remains legible under supported sizes, Bold Text, and text enlargement; use compatible system body/caption typography when needed. Remove repeated logos that displace useful content. A launch screen should provide startup continuity; a substantive brand introduction belongs in a welcome/onboarding moment. Check supplied app names/images for prohibited Apple marks rather than treating marketing branding as automatic trademark permission.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a bakery app replaces Back with its croissant logo, repeats a large wordmark over each list, and colors every button orange. Decision: navigation needs familiar meaning and orders need priority. After, a conventional Back control returns, the wordmark appears only where identification matters, warm photography supplies personality, and orange emphasizes the primary order action.

Deliver the revised screen/copy/token decisions or implementation, tying each brand change to a task consequence. Fail if the main content loses space to repeated identity, equivalent controls behave differently, or the custom font cannot expose a required label at supported settings. Call font/device/rendering checks pending when only static evidence exists.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for custom-font accommodation, [Color](../apple-hig-color/SKILL.md) for accent semantics, or [App icons](../apple-hig-app-icons/SKILL.md) when the identity surface is a launcher icon.

# Branding Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/branding) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Brand identity should remain recognizable while the app uses the platform’s established interaction conventions. App Store presentation is another branding opportunity governed by Apple’s marketing guidance. ## Best practices - Carry an intentional voice and tone through labels, guidance, and messages; vocabulary, sentence form, punctuation, and emoji can convey character. - Use accent color for meaningful emphasis such as primary actions, unread badges, or selected tabs. Consider expressing richer brand color in scrolling content that informs the Liquid Glass layer instead of coloring many controls. - If a brand font is necessary, verify legibility at all supported sizes, Bold Text, and Dynamic Type. Custom headings with system body/caption fonts can preserve character and readability. - Customize familiar components without losing expected size, location, or behavior. Preserve conventional symbols, navigation, and modality even in highly stylized interfaces. - Make content the priority. Avoid repeated logos or brand-only screen elements that displace useful information; add a logo only when context requires it. - Keep launch screens focused on startup continuity. Use a welcome or onboarding experience if a meaningful brand introduction is needed. - Follow Apple trademark guidance; Apple marks must not appear in app names or images. ## Platform considerations The source applies these principles across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS without additional platform rules. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/branding) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026.

I’ll specify a simple journal mark shared across iPhone and Mac, remove the tagline and seasonal badge, and leave masking and lighting to the system. Rendering and export checks will remain pending until artwork exists.
